zh.summary: 透過完整 Northstar 案例與七張雙語示意圖，理解跨管道冒充、OTP 轉交、抗釣魚驗證、獨立查證與事件證據，並連結 CEH 的防護與應變知識。

sourceBody.text: CEH M09-03｜語音釣魚、簡訊釣魚與身分冒充
Module 09：Social Engineering（社交工程）｜初學者教學｜約 12–15 分鐘
本課最重要的觀念：攻擊者不一定需要破解你的電腦，只要讓你誤以為他是可信任的人，就可能誘導你親手完成不安全的操作。
而且，收到兩則看似互相證明的訊息，不代表有兩個獨立的可信來源。
我們會透過一間虛構的 Northstar 教材中心，依序理解：

items: 1. 攻擊者怎麼利用簡訊、電話與假身分？
2. 為什麼真正的登入驗證碼，也可能變成攻擊工具？
3. 為什麼獨立查證比辨識聲音真假更可靠？
4. 資安人員如何結合 CEH 其他單元的觀念，分析、阻擋與調查攻擊？

sourceBody.text: 一、先建立全貌：釣魚攻擊其實有四個不同面向
上一課 M09-02 介紹了 Phishing（釣魚）、Spear Phishing（魚叉式／定向釣魚）與 Whaling（鯨釣）。
今天要加入三個新名詞：

items: Smishing：簡訊釣魚，使用簡訊誘導被害人。
Vishing：語音釣魚，透過電話或語音誘導被害人。
Impersonation：身分冒充，讓被害人誤認攻擊者是其他人或機構。

sourceBody.text: 這些不是互斥的攻擊分類。它們是在回答不同問題。

visual.caption: 圖 1｜本課建立的四維攻擊分析框架。
visual.description: 本課的分析工具：目標、管道、冒充身分、要求行動可以同時成立。

items.title: 鎖定誰？｜Target
items.body: 一般員工小林；是否有證據顯示特別針對他設計？

items.title: 從哪裡接觸？｜Channel
items.body: SMS 簡訊與 Voice 語音；同一場攻擊可以跨管道。

items.title: 假扮成誰？｜Identity
items.body: 自稱資訊服務台；假冒可信的客服角色。

items.title: 要求做什麼？｜Action
items.body: 交出登入驗證碼，或核准不是自己發起的登入。

sourceBody.text: 例如，攻擊者可能蒐集小林的背景資料，特別針對他設計簡訊，再以電話假冒公司客服，要求提供驗證碼。
如果確實有證據支持「量身設計」，我們就可以描述為：
定向釣魚（目標）＋簡訊與語音釣魚（管道）＋身分冒充（手法）＋取得驗證碼（目的）。
注意一個考試容易犯的錯誤：攻擊者自稱董事長，並不自動構成 Whaling。鯨釣主要是指鎖定高階或高價值人物，而不是冒充高階人物。

加拿大資安中心也將 Smishing、Vishing 等歸在社交工程及釣魚攻擊的相關類型。[加拿大資安中心：社交工程](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/social-engineering-itsap00166)；[語音釣魚](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/what-voice-phishing-vishing-itsap00102)；[簡訊釣魚](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/smishing-protect-yourself-sms-attacks-itsap00103)
二、Vishing 與 Smishing：兩個管道，可能只有一個攻擊者
想像你是 Northstar 教材中心的小林。
上午 10 點，你收到簡訊：
【Northstar 資訊服務台】偵測到您的教材帳號異常登入，請儘速聯繫客服，以免帳號停權。
兩分鐘後，電話響了。
對方說：「小林您好，我是資訊服務台。你現在負責的教材專案帳號有異常，我們剛才應該有發簡訊給你。」
小林心想：「他竟然知道我的名字、工作內容，還知道我剛收到簡訊。」
然而，真正可能發生的是：

visual.caption: 圖 2｜攻擊者可以同時控制簡訊和電話，製造彼此佐證的假象。
visual.description: 同一個攻擊者安排簡訊與電話，讓小林誤以為兩邊互相佐證。

items.title: 同一個攻擊者
items.body: 同時安排簡訊與語音接觸；控制來源沒有變成兩個。

items.title: 簡訊 SMS
items.body: 攻擊者傳送「帳號出現異常」，引導小林處理假事件。

items.title: 電話 Voice
items.body: 同一方來電自稱資訊客服，提到剛才的簡訊。

items.title: 小林收到兩段接觸
items.body: 一致說法可能只是同源安排，不能單獨證明客服身分。

sourceBody.text: 這個手法利用了人的一種直覺：當不同地方都出現一致資訊，我們容易認為可信度增加。
但從資安角度，關鍵是證據是否真正獨立。
三個需要分清楚的技術觀念

items: 1. Caller ID Spoofing（來電顯示偽冒）

sourceBody.text: 電話顯示的號碼或名稱，可能遭到偽冒。
就像寄信時，信封上寫「某某銀行寄出」，不代表你已經確認寄件者真的是銀行。
FTC 提醒，不能只根據來電顯示判定對方身分。[美國聯邦貿易委員會：來電顯示可以被偽冒](https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2016/05/scammers-can-fake-caller-id-info)

items: 2. AI Voice Cloning（AI 語音複製）

sourceBody.text: 攻擊者也可能使用 AI 模仿主管、親友或客服人員的聲音。[FTC：AI 語音複製詐騙](https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2023/03/scammers-use-ai-enhance-their-family-emergency-schemes)
但要注意：

items: 聽起來像真人，不代表是真人。
聽起來像某個人，不代表真的是那個人。
聲音有失真，也不能直接認定使用了 AI。

sourceBody.text: 因此真正的防護策略，不是要求你練出一雙能百分之百辨認 AI 假聲音的耳朵，而是建立不依賴聲音本身的身分驗證程序。

items: 3. Reconnaissance（偵察）與 Footprinting（足跡蒐集）

sourceBody.text: 這裡可以連結 CEH M02 的相關概念。
攻擊者能叫出小林的姓名、部門與專案名稱，可能是因為事前從公司網站、社群貼文、活動名單等地方蒐集資訊。
如果是從系統服務查得具體帳號、群組或共享資訊，還可能連結 M04 的 Enumeration（列舉）。
但要嚴格區分：
知道一個人的背景，不代表攻擊者已經入侵他的帳號；知道內部專案名稱，也不直接證明資料曾經外洩。
三、真正的 OTP，怎麼會協助假客服？
這是整堂課最值得理解的技術機制。
OTP（One-Time Password，一次性密碼／驗證碼）原本是一種安全措施。

本課用 OTP 泛指這個案例的一次性登入碼。嚴格依 NIST 分類，平台傳到手機的簡訊碼屬於帶外驗證（Out-of-Band Authentication），與驗證器自行產生的 OTP 是不同類型；兩者若需要人手轉填，仍可能遭到誘騙轉交。[NIST SP 800-63B-4：驗證器與抗釣魚能力](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html#phishres)
假設你登入教材系統：

items: 1. 輸入帳號與密碼。
2. 系統要求第二項驗證。
3. 平台傳送一次性驗證碼到你的手機。
4. 你在自己發起的登入流程中輸入驗證碼，平台驗證通過後才可能允許登入。

sourceBody.text: 正常情況下，OTP 是在降低帳號遭盜用的風險。
但攻擊者可以利用社交工程，嘗試讓你把驗證碼交給他。

visual.caption: 圖 3｜一次性驗證碼的社交工程攻擊流程。這是合成情境，並非所有網站都採取相同驗證程序。
visual.description: 合成情境：驗證碼是真的，索取它的人卻可能是假的。每個平台的條件不同。

items.title: 攻擊者發起請求
items.body: 嘗試登入或帳號復原；仍須滿足平台的其他驗證條件。

items.title: 真正的平台發送 OTP
items.body: 平台把該次操作的驗證碼送到小林的手機。

items.title: 小林收到真碼與假電話
items.body: 手機收到真的 OTP；同時有人冒充客服要求念出它。

items.title: 小林把碼交給冒充者
items.body: 驗證碼由持有人轉交給攻擊者，而不是自行在可信入口使用。

items.title: 攻擊者嘗試提交驗證碼
items.body: 把碼送回真正的平台；是否成功仍取決於其他條件與實際紀錄。

sourceBody.text: 為什麼平台無法單靠 OTP 分辨是不是本人？
用白話來說：
平台檢查的是「這組驗證碼是否正確、有效、符合驗證規則」，不一定能知道輸入驗證碼的人是不是手機真正的持有人。
假設：

items: 攻擊者已取得小林的帳號密碼。
平台再要求一組簡訊驗證碼。
小林把驗證碼念給假客服。
攻擊者在有效期限內，把驗證碼提交給真正的平台。

sourceBody.text: 在其他驗證條件也成立時，攻擊者就可能成功登入。
這裡也要修正一個常見誤解：不是所有 OTP 只要被知道，就一定可以登入。 有些系統還有裝置限制、額外驗證、風險判定等條件；不同驗證碼也可能只對應特定操作。
接著理解 MFA 與抗釣魚驗證
MFA（Multi-Factor Authentication，多因素驗證）是要求不同類型的驗證因素。
例如：

rows: Something you know
你知道的密碼
Something you have
你持有的手機或安全金鑰
Something you are
你的指紋等生物特徵

sourceBody.text: 這裡的核心不是驗證步驟有幾個，而是有沒有使用不同類型的因素。兩組密碼不會因為輸入兩次，就自動變成 MFA。

NIST SP 800-63B-4 明確指出，需要手動輸入驗證輸出的 OTP 與帶外驗證，不屬於抗釣魚驗證（Phishing-resistant Authentication），因為手動輸入不會把驗證輸出綁定到正在驗證的特定工作階段（一段特定的驗證互動），攻擊者可能轉交該輸出。[NIST SP 800-63B-4：抗釣魚能力](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html#phishres)
進一步比較：

visual.caption: 圖 4｜抗釣魚能力不等於只是增加一個驗證步驟。
visual.description: 比較的是驗證輸出能否被轉交，以及它是否綁定正確的驗證對象。

items.title: 傳統 OTP
items.body: 本例的簡訊驗證碼有期限、只能使用一次，仍可能被即時轉交給攻擊者。

items.title: 抗釣魚驗證
items.body: 例如正確實作的 FIDO2／WebAuthn 驗證，透過密碼學機制綁定驗證對象。

sourceBody.text: Passkey（通行密鑰）是基於 FIDO 標準的密碼學登入憑證，常透過 WebAuthn 使用；但完整服務的保護仍要看具體實作、帳號復原及使用情境。抗釣魚驗證主要防止登入憑證被假網站利用，不會自動阻擋所有詐騙付款或不當資料授權。[FIDO Alliance：Passkeys](https://fidoalliance.org/passkeys/)
再連到 Authentication 與 Authorization
這裡要建立資安工程最基本的區分：

items: Authentication（身分驗證）：你是誰？你能否證明自己控制這個帳號？
Authorization（授權）：你通過身分驗證後，可以做什麼？

sourceBody.text: 就像進辦公室要先刷員工證，但進去之後，也不是每間主管辦公室、每個資料櫃都可以打開。
因此，登入成功不代表所有操作都有授權；攻擊者取得驗證碼，也不代表他已讀取全部資料。
四、Independent Verification：真正的查證，是離開對方控制的資訊來源
現在回到小林的案例。
假客服說：「如果你不相信我，可以回撥剛剛簡訊裡的客服電話。」
小林照做，接電話的人說：「對，剛才確實有一張異常登入工單。」
你覺得這樣完成查證了嗎？
沒有。因為客服號碼和工單資訊，可能全部都是攻擊者提供的。

visual.caption: 圖 5｜獨立查證最重要的是信任來源，不是更換通訊工具。
visual.description: 差別不在換了幾個 App 或問了幾次，而是是否離開可疑來源控制的聯絡方式。

items.title: 路線 A｜仍在可疑來源的圈子
items.body: 可疑簡訊 → 簡訊提供的客服連結 → 對方提供的客服號碼 → 對方聲稱確認成功。這仍沒有獨立證明。

items.title: 路線 B｜回到既有可信程序
items.body: 可疑簡訊 → 暫停、掛斷 → 自行開啟既有服務台 → 核對工單、身分與權限。只執行必要且已授權的操作。

sourceBody.text: 假設你收到有人冒充銀行客服的電話，正確做法是結束可疑通話，再自己開啟銀行原本就已安裝的官方 App，或使用之前已核實的官方聯絡方式查證。
在台灣，民眾也可以自行撥打 165 反詐騙諮詢專線，協助辨識可疑詐騙情境。這是刑事警察局提供的正式諮詢管道。[刑事警察局：165 反詐騙諮詢專線](https://www.cib.npa.gov.tw/ch/app/faq/view?id=18233&module=faq&serno=8306e5f3-6b7a-45e9-9d21-af24d4fac9af)
但要進一步記住：即使確認來電者真的在公司工作，也不代表他的每一項要求都有授權。
例如真正的資訊人員要求你寄出全公司員工資料，也需要檢查工作目的、權限與正式核准流程。
所以我們要分成三件事：身分是真的嗎？要求是真的嗎？操作有獲得授權嗎？
五、資安事件判讀：交出驗證碼，不等於已經完成入侵
這裡直接連結先前 M01-07 的 Incident Response（資安事件應變）。
假設小林向資安人員報告：「我接到假客服電話，好像把驗證碼唸給他了。」
資安工程師不能直接寫：
「攻擊者已經入侵公司，所有教材資料全部外洩。」
因為目前的證據只能支持更有限的結論。

visual.caption: 圖 6｜事件發展與證據層次。實務上各階段可能重疊、跳過或尚無法確認。
visual.description: 這些是不同的證據問題，不是必然依序發生的攻擊階段；可能重疊、跳過或仍無法確認。

items.title: 接觸
items.body: 簡訊與通話紀錄：能證明有接觸跡象，不能單靠顯示資訊確認身分。

items.title: 憑證暴露
items.body: 員工表示說出 OTP：有驗證資訊暴露風險，應立即依風險處置。

items.title: 驗證成功
items.body: 平台驗證或登入紀錄：仍須核對操作者與授權，不能直接認定是攻擊者。

items.title: 未授權操作
items.body: 存取或變更紀錄：核實操作者、工作目的、權限及實際行為。

items.title: 資料外流
items.body: 經核實的傳輸證據：確認資料內容、接收方及範圍，不能只靠下載警示定案。

sourceBody.text: 現在用實際的證據思考：

rows: 簡訊截圖與通話紀錄
確實有訊息與通話的跡象，還不能確認來源身分
小林表示已唸出 OTP
有驗證資訊暴露風險，需要立即處理
平台顯示成功登入
有登入成功事件，仍要確認是否為未授權登入
異常裝置存取、下載紀錄
有值得調查的存取行為，需確認操作者及目的
經核實的資料傳輸證據
才能進一步支持資料外流判斷，並評估範圍

sourceBody.text: 風險處置可以先於完整調查，但最終結論不能超越證據。
如果小林真的把驗證碼交給陌生人，應立即透過正式服務台通報。視系統情況，由授權人員檢查登入紀錄、終止可疑工作階段、更新必要憑證，並保全日誌。
如果沒有看到登入紀錄，也不能保證絕對安全，因為紀錄可能不完整或尚未查到正確來源。
這其實就是 M01-07 教過的原則：先限制可能的損害，再調查、復原與改善。
六、把本課連接到前面 CEH 的知識地圖
現在最重要的不是再背更多縮寫，而是理解相關概念怎麼一起運作。

visual.caption: 圖 7｜將 M09-03 放回整體 CEH 的知識架構，而不是單獨背誦三個新名詞。
visual.description: 概念關聯，不是固定攻擊順序。合法授權與交戰規則約束整個測試與調查過程。

items.title: M09｜社交工程
items.body: 辨認釣魚、身分冒充與跨管道信任。

items.title: M02／M04｜偵察與列舉
items.body: 蒐集目標與環境線索；有線索不等於已入侵。

items.title: M01-04／05｜攻擊分析
items.body: 從攻擊向量與實際行為分析；ATT&CK 分類不是成功證明。

items.title: M01-01／02｜安全與風險
items.body: CIA、資產、威脅、弱點與後果。

items.title: M01-06｜防護措施
items.body: 身分驗證、最小權限與縱深防禦。

items.title: M01-07｜事件應變
items.body: 偵測、圍堵、調查、復原與改善。

items.title: M01-03｜合法授權與 ROE
items.body: 安全測試與調查都必須在明確授權與範圍內。

sourceBody.text: 再深入兩個最重要的連結
第一個：M01-05 MITRE ATT&CK。
M01-05 說明了：MITRE ATT&CK 不只是把攻擊分階段，而是用 Tactics（戰術目的）與 Techniques（技術行為）描述攻擊。
針對目標使用語音誘導他提供存取權限，能與 ATT&CK 的 [T1566.004 — Spearphishing Voice](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/004/) 對應。這項技術位於 Initial Access（初始存取）的戰術範疇。
但不能因為看到一通假客服電話，就認定攻擊者已成功取得初始存取權限。ATT&CK 的技術分類是在描述行為，事件成功程度仍要用證據確認。
第二個：M01-06 Defense in Depth（縱深防禦）。
假設 Northstar 要防止這類事件，不能只靠教育員工「不要相信陌生電話」。
應同時安排不同層次的措施：

rows: 人員與流程
既有查證管道、可疑要求通報、敏感操作複核
帳號與驗證
適當採用抗釣魚 MFA、異常登入監控
權限管理
最小權限（Least Privilege）、重大變更另行核准
裝置保護
遠端協助工具須經正式授權
偵測與應變
日誌、異常告警、工作階段撤銷與事件調查

sourceBody.text: 這就是縱深防禦的價值：即使小林一時做出錯誤判斷，還有其他控制措施降低攻擊成功與損害擴大的可能性。
從 M01-01 的 CIA Triad 來看，未授權讀取教材資料可能危害機密性（Confidentiality）；擅自修改課程成績可能危害完整性（Integrity）；帳號遭鎖定使工作中斷，則可能危害可用性（Availability）。
七、兩分鐘小實驗：親自判斷可信來源
不用安裝 Kali Linux、不需要執行指令，也不需要真的傳簡訊。
假設有人自稱銀行客服，要求你提供手機收到的登入驗證碼。你要如何查證？
A. 回撥對方簡訊提供的客服號碼
B. 自行開啟先前確認的官方銀行 App，從既有入口查詢
C. 請來電者再說一次自己的員工編號
請先選擇並說出理由，再展開參考解答。這是桌上練習，不會送出答案，也不代表已完成理解驗收。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：1. 兩分鐘小實驗：哪個查證方式比較可靠？
paragraphs: 參考答案是 B：自行開啟先前確認的官方銀行 App，從既有入口查詢。關鍵不是「App 一定比電話安全」，而是這個入口不是這次可疑來電或簡訊臨時指定的。
A 仍然使用可疑來源提供的號碼。即使接電話的人說「確實是我們」，也可能只是同一方安排的另一段話，不能當成獨立證明。
C 要求對方再說一次員工編號，也沒有離開對方控制的資訊來源。對方說得出編號，不等於你已從可信系統查到這個人、工單與要求。
實際處理時，先不提供登入驗證碼，結束可疑通話，再使用自己既有的可信聯絡方式確認身分、要求與授權。即使確認是銀行人員，也不要因此省略敏感操作的正常程序。[加拿大資安中心：語音釣魚的防護](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/what-voice-phishing-vishing-itsap00102)

sourceBody.text: 八、課後理解檢核
下面三題涵蓋本課的攻擊分類、驗證機制與事件應變。先用自己的話思考，不需要寫很長。
第 1 題｜攻擊分類
攻擊者針對一名公司財務主管，先傳送釣魚簡訊，再打電話假冒銀行客服。這個事件可能同時涉及哪些釣魚概念？為什麼？
第 2 題｜技術原理
為什麼真正的平台產生的 OTP，仍可能協助攻擊者完成登入？為什麼這不代表 MFA 完全沒有用？
第 3 題｜事件處置
員工確實說出 OTP，但目前只有通話紀錄，尚無登入與存取日誌。你可以確認哪些事？不能確認哪些事？第一步應如何處理？
請先用自己的話回答三題，再逐題對照參考解答。參考解答是教學資料，不是學習者已提交的答案或已確認的理解紀錄。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：2. 課後第 1 題：這起事件可以有哪些分類？
paragraphs: 這些概念可以同時成立：簡訊管道對應 Smishing，電話中的欺騙性誘導對應 Vishing，假扮銀行客服則是 Impersonation。它們分別描述管道與手法，不是互斥選項；整體仍屬於 Phishing 的範圍。
從目標角度看，題目明確鎖定公司財務主管，可描述為針對特定目標的 Spear Phishing。如果這位主管具有高階職位、重大付款決策權或其他高價值權限，還可能更精確地稱為 Whaling。不要只因「主管」兩字就補出題目沒有提供的職級或權限。
重點是分清楚「攻擊誰」與「冒充誰」。這裡被鎖定的是財務主管，冒充的是銀行客服；不是因為攻擊者用了某個顯得重要的身分，事件才算鯨釣。實際事件仍應先核對目標、內容與行為，再選擇有證據支持的分類。[加拿大資安中心：社交工程](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/social-engineering-itsap00166)

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：3. 課後第 2 題：真 OTP 為什麼還可能幫助攻擊者？
paragraphs: 驗證碼是真的，只能說明它來自真正的平台或符合驗證規則；不能替索取驗證碼的人證明身分。若攻擊者已掌握其他必要條件，又誘導使用者交出仍有效的碼，就可能把它提交給真正的平台，完成那次驗證。
但「取得碼」不等於「一定登入成功」。仍要看碼對應哪項操作、是否過期或已使用，以及裝置限制、額外驗證和其他條件是否成立。成功與否必須用實際紀錄確認，不能只憑這個機制示意推定。

這不代表 MFA 沒有用。不同因素能增加保護，例如只有密碼外洩時，額外因素可能阻止登入；問題在於不同驗證方式的抗釣魚能力不同。需要人手轉填的 OTP 或簡訊帶外驗證輸出，可能被誘騙轉交，不應當成抗釣魚驗證。正確實作的 FIDO2／WebAuthn 則利用密碼學綁定驗證對象。[NIST SP 800-63B-4：抗釣魚能力](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html#phishres)
最後還要分開登入與授權：強化登入驗證，不會自動判斷每筆付款、每次資料交付都合理。仍需獨立核准與最小權限等其他控制。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：4. 課後第 3 題：可以下什麼結論，先做什麼？
paragraphs: 依題目前提，員工已把 OTP 說出去，應視為驗證資訊暴露風險；通話紀錄則能支持有相應通話活動。若是在真實調查中，通話紀錄本身不一定證明說話內容，仍要區分使用者陳述、其他佐證與已核實事實。
目前不能直接認定未授權登入已成功、帳號已被完整控制，或教材資料已經外洩。還要查碼對應的操作、有效性、驗證與登入結果、操作者是否獲授權，以及後續存取、下載或傳輸範圍。
第一步不是等到證據全部齊全才處理，而是停止可疑互動，不再提供碼或核准要求，立即從既有正式服務台通報。由有權負責的人員依風險保護帳號、檢查或撤銷可疑工作階段、處理必要憑證，並保留相關訊息、時間與日誌；不要自行清除紀錄或再次測試可疑內容。
之後再交叉核對登入、裝置、權限變更、服務工單與資料活動。找不到異常紀錄不代表絕對安全，也可能是紀錄不完整。白話總結就是：風險可以先處置，成功入侵與外洩則要各自取得證據。[加拿大資安中心：社交工程事件應變](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/social-engineering-itsap00166)

sourceBody.text: 最後把 M09-03 收斂成一個完整思考模式：
先確認對方透過什麼管道接觸你、聲稱具有什麼身分、要求取得什麼權限；接著離開可疑來源獨立查證；如果已經發生危險操作，就先控制風險，再以證據判定實際影響。
這套方法不只適用於假客服電話，也適用於假檢警、冒充主管、帳號復原詐騙，以及未來遇到的 AI 語音冒充攻擊。
下一課 M09-04 的 Pretexting（情境編造）、Baiting（誘餌）和 Tailgating（尾隨進入），將會進一步說明：攻擊者如何設計一個合理情境，讓你主動幫他跨過原本存在的安全界線。

en.summary: Follow the full Northstar scenario and seven bilingual diagrams to understand cross-channel impersonation, OTP relay, phishing-resistant authentication, independent verification, and incident evidence in the wider CEH context.

sourceBody.text: CEH M09-03 | Vishing, Smishing, and Impersonation
Module 09: Social Engineering | Beginner lesson | About 12–15 minutes

The central idea of this lesson: attackers do not always need to break into your computer. If they make you believe they are someone trustworthy, they may persuade you to carry out an unsafe action yourself.
Also, receiving two messages that appear to confirm each other does not establish two independent, trustworthy sources.
Using the fictional Northstar Learning Center, we will work through these questions:

items: 1. How do attackers combine text messages, phone calls, and false identities?
2. Why can a genuine login code become useful to an attacker?
3. Why is independent verification more reliable than trying to recognize a fake voice?
4. How can security staff connect concepts from other CEH units to analyze, prevent, and investigate the attack?

sourceBody.text: 1. Start with the whole picture: four different dimensions of phishing
The previous unit, M09-02, introduced phishing, spear phishing, and whaling.
This lesson adds three terms:

items: Smishing: phishing that uses SMS text messages to manipulate the recipient.
Vishing: phishing that uses telephone or other voice communication to manipulate the recipient.
Impersonation: causing a person to mistake an attacker for another person or organization.

sourceBody.text: These are not mutually exclusive attack categories. They answer different questions.

visual.caption: Figure 1 | The four-dimensional attack-analysis framework used in this lesson.
visual.description: A teaching framework: target, channel, claimed identity and requested action can coexist.

items.title: Who is targeted?
items.body: Lin, an ordinary employee. Is there evidence of content tailored to him?

items.title: Which channel?
items.body: SMS and voice. One attack may use more than one channel.

items.title: Who is impersonated?
items.body: The caller claims to be the IT help desk, borrowing trust in that role.

items.title: What is requested?
items.body: Disclose a login code or approve a login the employee did not initiate.

sourceBody.text: For example, an attacker might gather background information about Lin, design a text specifically for him, then call while pretending to be company support and ask for a verification code.
If there is actual evidence that the approach was tailored to him, we can describe it as:
Spear phishing (target) + smishing and vishing (channels) + impersonation (technique) + obtaining a verification code (objective).

A common exam mistake: an attacker claiming to be a chairperson does not automatically make the incident whaling. Whaling primarily concerns targeting senior or high-value people, not impersonating a senior person.

The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security also places smishing and vishing among related forms of social engineering and phishing. [Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: Social engineering](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/social-engineering-itsap00166); [Vishing](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/what-voice-phishing-vishing-itsap00102); [Smishing](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/smishing-protect-yourself-sms-attacks-itsap00103)
2. Vishing and smishing: two channels may have one attacker behind them
Imagine that you are Lin at Northstar Learning Center.
At 10 a.m., you receive a text:
[Northstar IT Help Desk] An unusual login has been detected on your course-materials account. Contact support promptly to avoid account suspension.
Two minutes later, your phone rings.
The caller says, “Hello, Lin. This is the IT help desk. There is an issue with the account for the course-materials project you are managing. We should have just sent you a text.”
Lin thinks, “They know my name, my work, and even that I just received a text.”
But this is what might actually be happening:

visual.caption: Figure 2 | An attacker can control both the text message and the phone call, creating an illusion of mutual confirmation.
visual.description: One attacker arranges both the text and the call, making them appear to corroborate each other.

items.title: One attacker
items.body: The same source controls both the SMS and the voice contact.

items.title: SMS
items.body: The attacker sends an account-alert text to draw Lin into a fabricated incident.

items.title: Voice call
items.body: The same party claims to be IT support and refers to the earlier text.

items.title: Lin receives both
items.body: Matching claims may share one source; they do not independently verify support.

sourceBody.text: This approach exploits an intuitive response: when consistent information appears in different places, we tend to treat it as more credible.
From a security perspective, however, the important question is whether the evidence is genuinely independent.
Three technical ideas to distinguish

items: 1. Caller ID spoofing

sourceBody.text: The name or number displayed for an incoming call can be falsified.
It is like writing “sent by a bank” on an envelope: that label does not establish that the bank really sent it.

The FTC warns against relying on caller ID alone to establish who is calling. [Federal Trade Commission: Scammers can fake caller ID info](https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2016/05/scammers-can-fake-caller-id-info)

items: 2. AI voice cloning

sourceBody.text: Attackers may also use AI to imitate the voice of a manager, family member, friend, or support worker. [FTC: AI voice-cloning scams](https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2023/03/scammers-use-ai-enhance-their-family-emergency-schemes)
Keep these distinctions in mind:

items: Sounding human does not prove that the voice is a live human voice.
Sounding like a particular person does not prove that the speaker is that person.
Distorted audio does not by itself prove that AI was used.

sourceBody.text: The real defensive strategy is therefore not to develop perfect hearing for every AI-generated voice. It is to establish identity-verification procedures that do not depend on the voice alone.

items: 3. Reconnaissance and footprinting

sourceBody.text: This connects to concepts in CEH M02.
An attacker who knows Lin's name, department, and project may previously have collected that information from a company website, social posts, event lists, or similar sources.
If specific account, group, or shared-resource information was obtained by querying system services, the activity may also connect to enumeration in M04.
But keep a firm distinction:
Knowing someone's background does not prove that their account has been compromised. Knowing an internal project name also does not directly establish that information was leaked.
3. How can a genuine OTP help a fake support worker?
This is the technical mechanism most worth understanding in the lesson.
An OTP, or one-time password/verification code, is intended as a security measure.

This lesson uses OTP informally for the one-time login code in the example. Under NIST's formal classification, a code that a platform sends to a phone by SMS belongs to out-of-band authentication, which differs from an OTP generated by an authenticator. If people must manually enter either kind of output, they may still be deceived into relaying it. [NIST SP 800-63B-4: Authenticators and phishing resistance](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html#phishres)
Suppose you are logging into the course-materials system:

items: 1. You enter your account name and password.
2. The system requires a second authentication factor.
3. The platform sends a one-time verification code to your phone.
4. You enter the code in the login process you initiated. Only after verification succeeds may the platform permit the login.

sourceBody.text: Under normal conditions, the OTP helps reduce the risk of account misuse.
An attacker can nevertheless use social engineering to try to persuade you to give them the code.

visual.caption: Figure 3 | Social engineering of a one-time verification code. This is a synthetic scenario; not every website uses the same authentication procedure.
visual.description: Synthetic scenario: the code is real, but the person requesting it may be an impostor. Platform rules differ.

items.title: Attacker starts a request
items.body: Attempts login or account recovery; the platform still requires its other conditions.

items.title: Real platform sends the OTP
items.body: The platform sends a code for that operation to Lin's phone.

items.title: Lin receives a real code and a fake call
items.body: A genuine OTP arrives while an impostor claiming to be support asks Lin to read it out.

items.title: Lin discloses the code to the impostor
items.body: The account holder relays the code to the attacker instead of using a trusted entry point.

items.title: Attacker attempts to submit the code
items.body: The code is sent to the real platform. Success depends on other conditions and the actual records.

sourceBody.text: Why can the platform not identify the person from the OTP alone?
In plain language:
The platform checks whether the code is correct, valid, and consistent with its verification rules. That does not necessarily reveal whether the person entering it is the actual holder of the phone.
Suppose that:

items: The attacker already has Lin's account name and password.
The platform also requires an SMS verification code.
Lin reads the code to the fake support worker.
The attacker submits it to the genuine platform while it is still valid.

sourceBody.text: If the other authentication conditions are also satisfied, the attacker may successfully log in.

This corrects a common misconception: knowing an OTP does not always guarantee a successful login. Some systems impose device restrictions, additional verification, or risk checks. Different codes may also authorize only particular operations.
Next, understand MFA and phishing-resistant authentication
MFA, or multi-factor authentication, requires different types of authentication factors.
For example:

rows: Something you know
A password you know
Something you have
A phone or security key you possess
Something you are
A biometric characteristic, such as your fingerprint

sourceBody.text: The key is not the number of steps, but whether different types of factors are used. Entering two passwords does not automatically make the process MFA.

NIST SP 800-63B-4 states that OTP and out-of-band authentication involving manual entry of an authenticator output are not phishing-resistant. Manual entry does not bind the output to the specific session being authenticated—a particular authentication interaction—so an attacker may relay it. [NIST SP 800-63B-4: Phishing resistance](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html#phishres)
Compare the two approaches:

visual.caption: Figure 4 | Phishing resistance is not simply an additional authentication step.
visual.description: Compare whether the authentication output can be relayed and whether it is bound to the intended verifier.

items.title: Traditional OTP
items.body: The SMS code in this example expires and can be used only once, but it may still be relayed to an attacker in real time.

items.title: Phishing-resistant authentication
items.body: Correctly implemented FIDO2/WebAuthn authentication, for example, uses cryptographic mechanisms to bind authentication to the intended verifier.

sourceBody.text: A passkey is a cryptographic sign-in credential based on FIDO standards, commonly used through WebAuthn. The protection of the complete service still depends on its implementation, account-recovery procedures, and usage context. Phishing-resistant authentication primarily prevents fake sites from exploiting login credentials; it does not automatically stop every fraudulent payment or improper authorization to release information. [FIDO Alliance: Passkeys](https://fidoalliance.org/passkeys/)
Connect this to authentication and authorization
This is a fundamental distinction in security engineering:

items: Authentication: Who are you? Can you demonstrate control of this account?
Authorization: Once authenticated, what are you permitted to do?

sourceBody.text: It is like using a staff badge to enter an office: getting through the entrance does not mean you can open every manager's office or every records cabinet.
A successful login therefore does not authorize every operation. An attacker obtaining a verification code also does not establish that all information has been read.
4. Independent verification means leaving the suspicious source's control
Return to Lin's situation.
The fake support worker says, “If you do not believe me, call the support number in the text you just received.”
Lin does so. The person answering says, “Yes, there was an unusual-login support ticket.”
Has this verified the request?
No. The support number and the ticket information may all have come from the attacker.

visual.caption: Figure 5 | Independent verification depends on the source of trust, not on switching communication tools.
visual.description: Changing apps or asking again is not enough if the suspicious source supplies every contact detail.

items.title: Path A | Still inside the same source
items.body: Suspicious SMS → support link in that SMS → phone number supplied by that contact → a claim of confirmation. There is still no independent proof.

items.title: Path B | Return to an established process
items.body: Suspicious SMS → pause and hang up → independently open the established help desk → verify the ticket, identity and authority. Perform only needed, authorized actions.

sourceBody.text: Suppose someone calls while impersonating your bank's support staff. A safer response is to end the suspicious call, then open the bank's official app that you already had installed, or use an official contact method you previously verified.

In Taiwan, people can also independently dial the 165 anti-fraud consultation hotline for help with suspected scams. It is an official consultation channel provided by the Criminal Investigation Bureau. [Criminal Investigation Bureau: 165 anti-fraud consultation hotline](https://www.cib.npa.gov.tw/ch/app/faq/view?id=18233&module=faq&serno=8306e5f3-6b7a-45e9-9d21-af24d4fac9af)
Remember one further distinction: even confirming that the caller really works for the company does not authorize every request they make.
For example, if a genuine IT employee asks you to send all employee records, you must still check the work purpose, permissions, and formal approval process.
Separate three questions: Is the identity genuine? Is the request genuine? Is the operation authorized?
5. Incident reasoning: sharing a code does not prove completed compromise
This connects directly to incident response in M01-07.
Suppose Lin tells security staff, “I received a call from fake support, and I think I read them my verification code.”
A security engineer cannot immediately write:
“The attacker has compromised the company, and all course materials have been disclosed.”
The current evidence supports a more limited conclusion.

visual.caption: Figure 6 | Incident developments and evidence levels. In practice, stages may overlap, be skipped, or remain unverified.
visual.description: These are evidence questions, not an inevitable attack sequence. Events may overlap, be absent or remain unconfirmed.

items.title: Contact
items.body: Texts and call records show signs of contact, not necessarily the caller's true identity.

items.title: Credential exposure
items.body: An employee reports sharing an OTP. This creates exposure risk requiring timely protective action.

items.title: Successful authentication
items.body: Platform records still need checks of the operator and authorization; success alone does not identify an attacker.

items.title: Unauthorized action
items.body: Verify the operator, purpose, permissions and actual activity using access or change records.

items.title: Data exfiltration
items.body: Verified transfer evidence must establish content, recipient and scope. A download alert alone is insufficient.

sourceBody.text: Now reason from the available evidence:

rows: A text-message screenshot and call record
There are signs of a message and call; the source's identity is not yet established
Lin reports having read out the OTP
Authentication information may have been exposed, requiring prompt action
The platform shows a successful login
A successful-login event exists; determine whether it was unauthorized
Unusual device access or download records
Access activity warrants investigation; identify the operator and purpose
Verified evidence of data transmission
This can further support a finding of data exfiltration and help establish its scope

sourceBody.text: Risk reduction can begin before an investigation is complete, but final conclusions must not exceed the evidence.

If Lin really shared the code with a stranger, he should report promptly through the official help desk. Depending on the system, authorized staff can examine login records, terminate suspicious sessions, update necessary credentials, and preserve logs.
Absence of an observed login record does not guarantee safety: records may be incomplete, or investigators may not yet have located the relevant source.
This is the principle described in M01-07: first limit potential harm, then investigate, recover, and improve.
6. Connect this lesson to the broader CEH knowledge map
The priority is not memorizing more abbreviations. It is understanding how the related concepts work together.

visual.caption: Figure 7 | Place M09-03 in the wider CEH knowledge structure instead of memorizing three isolated terms.
visual.description: Concept relationships, not a fixed attack sequence. Authorization and rules of engagement govern testing and investigation.

items.title: M09 | Social engineering
items.body: Recognize phishing, impersonation and cross-channel trust.

items.title: M02/M04 | Reconnaissance and enumeration
items.body: Gather target and environment clues; clues do not prove compromise.

items.title: M01-04/05 | Attack analysis
items.body: Analyze vectors and observed behavior. An ATT&CK classification is not proof of success.

items.title: M01-01/02 | Security and risk
items.body: CIA, assets, threats, vulnerabilities and consequences.

items.title: M01-06 | Defensive controls
items.body: Authentication, least privilege and defense in depth.

items.title: M01-07 | Incident response
items.body: Detect, contain, investigate, recover and improve.

items.title: M01-03 | Authorization and ROE
items.body: Testing and investigation must stay within explicit permission and scope.

sourceBody.text: Explore the two most important connections
First: MITRE ATT&CK in M01-05.
M01-05 explains that MITRE ATT&CK is not merely a way to divide attacks into stages. It describes attacks through tactics—the objectives—and techniques—the behaviors used.

Using voice communication to persuade a target to provide access can correspond to ATT&CK's [T1566.004 — Spearphishing Voice](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/004/). This technique belongs to the Initial Access tactic.

A fake-support call alone, however, does not prove that the attacker successfully obtained initial access. An ATT&CK technique classification describes behavior; the outcome of an incident still requires evidence.
Second: defense in depth in M01-06.
To prevent this type of incident, Northstar cannot rely only on telling employees, “Do not trust calls from strangers.”
It should arrange controls at multiple layers:

rows: People and process
Established verification channels, suspicious-request reporting, review of sensitive actions
Accounts and authentication
Appropriate phishing-resistant MFA, monitoring for unusual logins
Permission management
Least privilege and separate approval for major changes
Device protection
Formal authorization for remote-support tools
Detection and response
Logs, unusual-activity alerts, session revocation, and incident investigation

sourceBody.text: That is the value of defense in depth: even if Lin makes a poor decision in the moment, other controls can reduce the likelihood of attack success and wider harm.

Viewed through M01-01's CIA triad, unauthorized reading of course materials may harm confidentiality; improper alteration of course grades may harm integrity; and an account lockout that interrupts work may harm availability.
7. A two-minute exercise: identify a trustworthy source
You do not need to install Kali Linux, run commands, or send real text messages.
Suppose a caller claims to be bank support and asks for a login code received on your phone. How should you verify the request?
A. Call the support number provided in the caller's text
B. Independently open the official banking app you previously verified and use its established entry point
C. Ask the caller to repeat their employee number
Choose an answer and explain your reasoning before opening the reference explanation. This is a tabletop exercise: it does not submit an answer or establish verified understanding.

sourceBody.summary: Reference explanation: 1. Two-minute exercise: which verification method is more reliable?
paragraphs: The suggested answer is B: independently open the official banking app you previously verified and use its established entry point. The key is not that an app is always safer than a phone call. It is that the suspicious caller or text did not supply this entry point for the current interaction.

A still uses a number provided by the suspicious source. Even if the person answering says, “Yes, that was us,” it may simply be another part of the same party's arrangement, not independent evidence.

C asks the caller to repeat an employee number but remains inside the caller's information source. Knowing a number does not establish that a trusted system confirms the person, support ticket, or request.

In practice, do not provide the login code. End the suspicious call, then use an established trusted contact method to verify the identity, request, and authority. Even verifying a bank employee's identity does not remove the normal procedures for sensitive operations. [Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: Avoiding vishing](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/what-voice-phishing-vishing-itsap00102)

sourceBody.text: 8. After-lesson understanding check
These three questions cover attack classification, authentication mechanisms, and incident response. Think through each in your own words; a short answer is enough.
Question 1 | Attack classification
An attacker targets a company's finance manager, first sending a phishing text and then calling while impersonating bank support. Which phishing concepts might apply at the same time, and why?
Question 2 | Technical mechanism
Why can an OTP generated by the genuine platform still help an attacker log in? Why does this not mean that MFA is completely useless?
Question 3 | Incident handling

An employee definitely read out an OTP, but only call records are currently available; login and access logs have not yet been obtained. What can you establish? What can you not establish? What should be done first?

Answer the three questions in your own words, then compare each with its reference explanation. The explanations are teaching material, not records of a learner's submitted answers or verified understanding.

sourceBody.summary: Reference explanation: 2. After-lesson question 1: which classifications may apply?
paragraphs: These concepts can coexist: the SMS channel is smishing, deceptive inducement through the voice call is vishing, and pretending to be bank support is impersonation. They describe channels and a technique rather than mutually exclusive options. The overall activity remains within phishing.

From the target perspective, the question explicitly targets a company's finance manager, so spear phishing is an appropriate description. If that manager holds a senior position, substantial payment authority, or other high-value privileges, whaling may be a more specific classification. Do not infer an unstated rank or set of permissions solely from the word “manager.”

Distinguish whom the attacker targets from whom the attacker impersonates. The target is the finance manager; the claimed identity is bank support. An important-sounding assumed identity does not itself make an incident whaling. In a real investigation, examine the target, content, and behavior before applying the classifications supported by evidence. [Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: Social engineering](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/social-engineering-itsap00166)

sourceBody.summary: Reference explanation: 3. After-lesson question 2: how can a genuine OTP help an attacker?
paragraphs: A genuine code establishes only that it came from the real platform or satisfies its verification rules. It does not authenticate the person asking for it. If the attacker has the other required conditions and persuades the user to disclose a still-valid code, the attacker may submit it to the genuine platform and complete that authentication transaction.

Obtaining the code does not guarantee a successful login. The outcome depends on the operation associated with the code, whether it expired or was already used, and whether device restrictions, additional verification, and other conditions are satisfied. Confirm the outcome from actual records rather than inferring success from the mechanism alone.

This does not make MFA useless. Different factors add protection: for example, if only a password is exposed, an additional factor may prevent login. The limitation is that authentication methods differ in phishing resistance. Manually entered OTP or SMS out-of-band outputs can be relayed through deception and should not be treated as phishing-resistant. Correctly implemented FIDO2/WebAuthn instead uses cryptography to bind authentication to the intended verifier. [NIST SP 800-63B-4: Phishing resistance](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html#phishres)

Finally, keep login and authorization separate. Stronger authentication does not automatically establish that every payment or information disclosure is appropriate. Independent approval, least privilege, and other controls are still needed.

sourceBody.summary: Reference explanation: 4. After-lesson question 3: what can be concluded, and what comes first?
paragraphs: Under the question's stated premise, the employee read out the OTP, creating an authentication-information exposure risk. Call records support the occurrence of corresponding call activity. In a real investigation, call records do not necessarily establish what was said; separate the user's account, corroborating evidence, and verified facts.

You cannot yet conclude that unauthorized login succeeded, the account was fully controlled, or course materials were disclosed. Investigate the operation associated with the code, its validity, authentication and login results, whether the operator was authorized, and the scope of subsequent access, downloads, or transmissions.

Do not wait for every fact before taking protective action. Stop the suspicious interaction, provide no further codes or approvals, and report immediately through the established official help desk. Authorized responders can protect the account according to risk, inspect or revoke suspicious sessions, address necessary credentials, and preserve messages, timestamps, and logs. Do not erase records yourself or repeat suspicious actions as a test.

Then correlate login, device, permission-change, support-ticket, and data-activity records. A lack of observed anomalies does not guarantee safety because records may be incomplete. In short: address risk promptly, but establish successful compromise and data disclosure with their own evidence. [Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: Responding to social engineering](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/social-engineering-itsap00166)

sourceBody.text: Finally, bring M09-03 together into one complete reasoning approach:

Identify the channel through which the person approached you, the identity they claim, and the access or authority they seek. Then independently verify outside the suspicious source's control. If an unsafe action has already occurred, control the risk first and use evidence to establish the actual impact.
This approach applies not only to fake-support calls, but also to impersonated police or prosecutors, fake managers, account-recovery scams, and future AI voice-impersonation attempts.
The next unit, M09-04, covers pretexting, baiting, and tailgating. It explains how attackers construct a plausible situation that encourages someone to help them cross an existing security boundary.
